analysis.explanation: A fictional claim of a grandson in jail asks for an urgent payment and secrecy.

questioning.title: Pause and Think
questioning.message: Have you contacted your family member using a phone number you trusted before receiving this message?

authority.title: What Experts Recommend
authority.message: FTC guidance recommends checking a claimed family emergency by contacting the person through a known number and asking another trusted family member. This is general advice, not an assessment of this particular message by the institution.

source.name: Federal Trade Commission
source.label: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money

social_influence.title: Recognize the Scam Pattern
social_influence.message: Documented family-emergency scams involve someone posing as a relative who needs help. The scenario identified by the analysis warrants checking that possibility. Pressure to act quickly is a documented scam tactic. Requests for secrecy can discourage independent checks in documented emergency scams. Requests to pay with gift cards resemble a documented scam payment pattern. The payment-related concern in the analysis is a reason to independently check the recipient and payment method. These similarities do not establish that fraud occurred.

diversion.title: Take a Safer Step
diversion.message: Check the claimed emergency through family contacts you already trust before deciding whether to pay.

actions.label: Call the family member using a previously saved phone number.
Ask another trusted family member to help check the story.
Wait to send money until you have independently checked the request.
Do not share gift card numbers or PINs in response to this request. Verify it independently first.

analysis.explanation: A fictional bank warning threatens an account freeze and asks the recipient to follow a link.

questioning.title: Pause and Think
questioning.message: Have you checked this request through your bank's official app or the number printed on your bank card?

authority.title: What Experts Recommend
authority.message: FTC guidance recommends checking a message with the organization through a phone number or website you already trust, instead of contact details supplied in the message. This is general advice, not an assessment of this particular message by the institution.

source.name: Federal Trade Commission
source.label: How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams

social_influence.title: Recognize the Scam Pattern
social_influence.message: Documented bank-impersonation messages pose as a bank to gain trust. The scenario identified by the analysis warrants checking the sender independently. Threats of adverse consequences can be used to pressure recipients in scams. Links identified in the analysis can resemble phishing attempts that steer recipients to an unverified channel. These similarities do not establish that fraud occurred.

diversion.title: Take a Safer Step
diversion.message: Check the request directly with your bank using an established channel.

actions.label: Open your bank's official app independently and check for the request.
Call the number printed on your bank card.
Use established bank contact details instead of any details supplied with the request.
Leave the message's link unopened; check the request through an official channel you open independently.

analysis.explanation: A fictional supplier request changes the payment destination.

questioning.title: Pause and Think
questioning.message: Have you confirmed the changed payment details with your usual contact at the supplier?

authority.title: What Experts Recommend
authority.message: FBI guidance recommends verifying payment requests and changes to account numbers or payment procedures directly with the known contact. This is general advice, not an assessment of this particular message by the institution.

social_influence.title: Recognize the Scam Pattern
social_influence.message: Documented invoice scams can imitate a supplier's request. The invoice-fraud classification warrants checking that possibility. Unexpected changes in payment instructions resemble a documented invoice-redirection tactic. These similarities do not establish that fraud occurred.

diversion.title: Take a Safer Step
diversion.message: Confirm the invoice and intended recipient with the supplier through an established contact.

actions.label: Call your usual supplier contact using a previously established number.
Confirm the changed banking details with your usual supplier contact before paying.
Wait to make the payment until those details have been independently checked.
